trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for body-fragment, tree-aware text extraction. All HTML API calls are documented: create_fragment(), next_token(), get_token_type(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), get_attribute(), get_current_depth(), and get_modifiable_text(). The single-pass stack walk is idiomatic, appends only #text token text, relies on decoded get_attribute()/get_modifiable_text() values, and uses is_string() so absent/boolean href values are excluded while empty-string href would remain valid.

Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and a single next_token() walk with explicit current-link state. All called HTML API methods are present in the rendered docs: create_fragment(), next_token(), get_token_type(), get_token_name(), get_current_depth(), get_attribute(), get_modifiable_text(), and is_tag_closer(). The depth-drop boundary and #text-only concatenation match the documented subtree-walk pattern, and is_string() handles null/true/empty-string attribute semantics.

Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() and documented token APIs only: next_token(), get_token_type(), get_token_name(), is_tag_closer(), get_attribute(), get_current_depth(), and get_modifiable_text(). It tracks anchor depth for descendant text and finalizes on A closers; this works for unclosed source anchors because WP_HTML_Processor emits virtual closers. It also correctly excludes valueless href via is_string() and uses decoded text APIs.

failure_analysis: There were no failed hidden cases: all three trials passed simple, no-href-excluded, entity-in-href-decoded, valueless-href, image-link-empty-text, entities-in-text, no-links, and unclosed-link, with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well in three places: the processor-choice guidance says WP_HTML_Processor is for structure, walking subtrees, and collecting element text; the next_token()/get_current_depth()/text-extraction guidance gives the needed recipe of a token walk bounded by depth and appending only #text via get_modifiable_text(); and the attribute docs describe string|true|null semantics plus decoded string values. Near-misses were small: trials 1 and 3 finalize links on A closers, so the unclosed-link case depends on virtual closers being emitted; the docs mention virtual closers and depth drops, but this behavior could be more concrete. Also, the decoded-attribute guarantee is clearest in the Tag Processor get_attribute() section, while the HTML Processor get_attribute() section mostly relies on inheritance and examples.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor page documents the return type and boolean/null examples, but the explicit statement that string attribute values are already decoded is easier to find in the Tag Processor page than in the Processor method section users naturally read for tree-aware extraction.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Repeat the inherited contract in the HTML Processor method docs: string values are decoded, valueless/boolean attributes return true, missing or unavailable attributes return null, and present empty values return ''. Add a short note that callers requiring a textual value should test is_string().

doc_gaps.problem: The docs discuss virtual closers and depth drops, but do not show a compact token sequence for an element whose source end tag is omitted. Implementers may be unsure whether finalizing on a closer handles unclosed-but-tree-closed elements.
doc_gaps.suggestion:
Add a small generic example showing that parsing '

text' or another omitted-end-tag fragment visits an opener, a #text token, and a virtual closer, and distinguish this from paused_at_incomplete_token() for a truly incomplete trailing syntax token.

doc_gaps.problem: The correct ordinary-text recipe is present in narrative guidance, but the method-level docs could make the boundary clearer for readers arriving directly at get_modifiable_text().
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a method-level note or example: for ordinary element text, record the opener depth, walk tokens while depth remains inside the element, append get_modifiable_text() only when get_token_type() is '#text', and ignore descendant markup/media and special-element opener text unless explicitly requested.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs state null/true/empty-string semantics, but the common filtering rule is implicit. A model could still use truthiness and accidentally exclude href='' or include valueless href=true.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general example for attributes that must have a string value: use is_string( $processor->get_attribute( $name ) ), not a truthiness check, because '' is a present string value and true means a valueless boolean attribute.
